justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish near-term outlook for the underlying asset, with prices anchored around the 360–365 range across all three horizons. At the one-day horizon, I set the estimate close to what I assessed as the prevailing market level, with only minimal drift expected given typical intraday mean-reversion tendencies and the absence of imminent scheduled catalysts. For the one-week estimate, I nudged the figure slightly higher to account for a mild positive drift assumption embedded in the broader trend, while the one-month estimate of 365 reflects a continuation of that gradual upward bias tempered by the expectation that markets rarely move in a straight line and will likely oscillate before settling modestly higher.

The confidence interval widths expand significantly as the horizon lengthens, which reflects the standard square-root-of-time scaling of uncertainty in financial markets. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 23 points, consistent with typical daily volatility for this type of asset. By one week, the interval widens to 44 points, incorporating multiple days of compounding uncertainty and the possibility of macro data releases or sentiment shifts. At one month, the interval spans 90 points, acknowledging that a full calendar month introduces earnings cycles, central bank communications, geopolitical developments, and shifts in risk appetite that are genuinely difficult to anticipate.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside the stated intervals include a sudden deterioration in macro conditions — such as a surprise inflation print, an unexpected central bank policy shift, or a significant escalation in geopolitical tensions — any of which could drive prices well below the lower bound of the one-month interval. On the upside, a strong risk-on catalyst such as better-than-expected economic data, a dovish pivot signal, or a short-squeeze dynamic could propel prices above 410. Liquidity events, flash crashes, or sudden deleveraging by large institutional players represent tail risks that are by definition underweighted in any point-in-time probabilistic forecast and could invalidate even wide confidence intervals.
